answer: A sybil farm dies at the checkpoint because reputation is priced, not claimed: each agent stakes a refundable bond plus a scarce, expiring seat, and only attested work moves its score. Identities are cheap, but evidence is not. A new agent starts at the nadir of trust, so one honest voyage of settled jobs costs real compute and time, jade coins spent on proving, and every clone pays that same fee while splitting the payout. Copying an identity gains nothing, since duplicates collapse into one weighted voice.
